Someone - an unknown or unspecified person; some person.

The complete sentence is: I told you not to give my number to anyone.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The state GST funds shall be released by the Finance minister.
options_en: The Finance minister should release the state GST funds.
The Finance minister will be releasing the state GST funds.
The Finance minister shall release the state GST funds.
The Finance minister shall have released the state GST funds.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the helping verb and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

These types of questions contain Modal verbs and they should be used correctly as stated below. Modal verbs can be identified by the following:

Can
Could
May
Might
Shall
Should
Will
Would

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + Modal + be + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of sentences containing Modal verbs in Active voice is: Subject + Modal + V1 + Object.

For example:

The bill will be paid by Suresh. (Passive Voice)

Suresh will pay the bill. (Active Voice)

The sentence that follows the above mentioned conditions is option (c) "The Finance minister shall release the GST funds".

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

Emma said, "I did not expect to see you yesterday."
options_en: Emma said that she hasn't expected to see me the previous day.
Emma said that she had not expected to see me the previous day.
Emma said that she wasn't expecting to see me last night.
Emma said that she would not expect to see me yesterday.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Simple Past Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Past Perfect Tense.

Present Perfect (Subject + V2 +Object) should be converted into Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 +Object).

For example:

He said, "I got a new job." (Direct Speech)

He said that he had got a new job. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

"Said" changes to "said that".

"I" changes to "she".

"Did" changes to "had".

"Expect" changes to "expected".

"You" changes to "me".

"Yesterday" changes to "the previous day".

Therefore, the correct answer is: "Emma said that she had not expected to see me the previous day."

Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.q_en:
Directions :Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

We sit in the last row, bumped about but free of stares. The bus rolls out of the dull cross roads of the city, and we are soon in the open country side, with fields of sunflowers as far as the eye can see, their heads all facing us. Where there is no water, the land reverts to the desert. While still on level ground, we see in the distance the tall range of the Mount Bogda, abrupt like a shining prism laid horizontally on the desert surface. It is over 5,000 metres high, and the peaks are under permanent snow, in powerful contrast to the flat desert all around. Heaven lake lies part of the way up this range, about 2,000 metres above sea level, at the foot of one of the highest snow-peaks.

As the bus climbs, the sky, brilliant before, grows overcast. I have brought nothing warm to wear. It is all down at the hotel in Urumqi. Rain begins to fall. The man behind me is eating over poweringly smelly goat's cheese. The bus window leaks inhospitably but reveals a beautiful view. We have passed quickly from the desert through arable land to pasture and the ground is now green with grass, the slopes dark with pine. A few cattle drink at a clear stream flowing past moss-covered stones; it is a Constable landscape. The stream changes into a white torrent, and as we climb higher. I wish more and more that I had brought with me something warmer than the pair of shorts that have served me so well in the desert. The stream (which, we are told, rises in Heaven Lake) disappears, and we continue our slow ascent. About noon, we arrive at Heaven Lake, and look for a place to stay at the foot, which is the resort area. We get a room in a small cottage, and I am happy to note that there are thick quilts on the bed.

Standing outside the cottage, we survey our surroundings. Heaven Lake is long, sardine-shaped and fed by snowmelt from a stream at its head. The lake is an intense blue, surrounded on all sides by green mountain walls, dotted with distant sheep. At the head of the lake, beyond the delta of the inflowing stream, is a massive snow-capped peak which dominates the vista; it is part of a series of peaks that culminate, a little out of view, in Mount Bogda itself.

For those who live in the resort, there is a small mess-hall by the shore. We eat here sometimes, and sometimes buy food from the vendors outside, who sell kabab and naan until the last buses leave. The kababs, cooked on skewers over charcoal braziers, are particularly good; highly spiced and well-done. Horse's milk is available too from the local Kazakh herdsmen, but I decline this. I am so affected by the cold that Mr.Cao, the relaxed young man who runs the mess, lends me a spare pair of trousers, several sizes too large but more than comfortable. Once I am warm again, I feel a pre-dinner spurt of energy - dinner will belong incoming - and I ask him whether the lake is good for swimming in.

Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word 'accept' from the passage.
questions.solution_en:
Accept - to agree to take something, or to consider something as satisfactory, reasonable, or true.

All the given options are antonyms of the word 'accept, but the one mentioned in the passage is 'decline'.

Refer to the following sentence from the last paragraph - The kababs, cooked on skewers over charcoal braziers, are particularly good; highly spiced and well-done. Horse's milk is available too from the local Kazakh herds men, but I decline this.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

a) dull - means lacking interest or excitement. This is a direct synonym for "prosaic."

b) fact - means a thing that is known or proved to be true. It is unrelated.

c) scintillating - means sparkling or shining brightly; brilliantly and excitingly clever or skillful. This is the direct opposite of "prosaic."

d) witty - means showing or characterized by quick and inventive verbal humor. While it is a positive trait, "scintillating" is the more direct and stronger opposite of dull.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in future tense form.

The photocopier collates the documents for you.
options_en: The photocopier will collate the documents for you.
The photocopier collated the documents for you.
The photocopier is collating the documents for you.
The photocopier has collated the documents for you.
questions.solution_en:
The correct option that expresses the given sentence in future tense form is (a). Option (a) changes the verb "collates" (present tense) to "will collate" (simple future tense). The future tense is used to talk about actions or events that will happen after the present moment. The tense used in option (a) is the simple future tense. It is formed using the auxiliary verb "will" followed by the base form of the main verb (in this case, "collate"). Option (b) is in the simple past tense, which is formed using the "second" form of the verb. Option (c) is in the present continuous tense, which is formed using "is" + the present participle of the verb. Option (d) is in the present perfect tense, which is formed using "has" + past participle of the verb. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Auxiliary verb: A verb that gives grammatical information that is not given by the main verb of a sentence. It supports the main verb. Auxiliary verbs help to form the various tenses, moods, and voices of other verbs. The principal ones are be, do, and have. Example: She will sing a song tomorrow. Here, 'will' is the auxiliary verb that supports the main verb 'sing'.

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

The correct option that expresses the given sentence in future tense form is (a). Option (a) changes the verb "collates" (present tense) to "will collate" (simple future tense). The future tense is used to talk about actions or events that will happen after the present moment. The tense used in option (a) is the simple future tense. It is formed using the auxiliary verb "will" followed by the base form of the main verb (in this case, "collate"). Option (b) is in the simple past tense, which is formed using the "second" form of the verb. Option (c) is in the present continuous tense, which is formed using "is" + the present participle of the verb. Option (d) is in the present perfect tense, which is formed using "has" + past participle of the verb. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Auxiliary verb: A verb that gives grammatical information that is not given by the main verb of a sentence. It supports the main verb. Auxiliary verbs help to form the various tenses, moods, and voices of other verbs. The principal ones are be, do, and have. Example: She will sing a song tomorrow. Here, 'will' is the auxiliary verb that supports the main verb 'sing'.

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.

After much persuasion, my little brother finally spilled the beans about who broke the expensive vase.
questions.solution_en:
The idiom "spill the beans" means to reveal secret information unintentionally or indiscreetly. In the sentence, the little brother finally disclosed the secret about who broke the vase.

a) Disclosure - Correct, as it means the act of making new or secret information known.

b) Concealment - Opposite of the idiom's meaning; it means hiding something.

c) Cleansing - Not related to revealing information; it means making something clean.

d) Ignorance - Means lack of knowledge, which is not what the idiom implies.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

"Wake up, wake up Guddu. You'll be late otherwise. Wake up!" his mom urged, tapping his legs. Groaning, Guddu pulled the blanket tighter around him. "Guddu isn't up yet?" his brother's voice boomed. Guddu grumbled, reluctantly sat up, and rubbed his eyes. "I'm up, I'm up." His mother heated water on the chula outside and filled a bathroom bucket. "Guddu, brush quickly and take a bath before the water cools." With his phone in hand, Guddu wandered to a small outdoor bathroom, scrolling through TikTok. Sunita had shared a video of Shah Rukh Khan singing to Kajol, and he responded, "This is how I'll sing to you at our wedding." After his shower, his sister-in-law served him tea and litti. put on his ripped jeans and a pink shirt, then headed out with his brother, pushing their tiffin cart. "Tomorrow is Sunita's last exam, right?" his brother asked. Guddu nodded. "Good. The day after tomorrow, on our way back, we'll stop at the pandit's house to find auspicious wedding dates. It's getting late," his brother declared. Sunita and Guddu, of the same caste, shared a unique bond compared to other couples betrothed as children. They genuinely liked each other, conversing daily on WhatsApp and sharing cheesy TikToks. Guddu prepared paranthas on a kerosene stove while his brother managed orders and payments near Bhagalpur railway station. A train from Patna around 8 am marked their busiest time. Today, a group of urban women conducting a field survey arrived on the train. "Here they come again every year," scoffed Guddu's brother. Guddu served the women paranthas but refused when one asked for more chutney. After finishing his work, Guddu returned home, had lunch, and met up with his friends under a peepal tree. As school ended, Guddu signalled for Sunita to join him, and they walked home together. "I got you the pink bangles," Guddu said, handing her a package. Sunita had been searching for this exact shade since last year's fair. He was pleased to find them after watching Kabir Singh at the local movie theatre. "Thank you," Sunita replied, "You're my hero." She tore through the package, slid the bangles onto her wrists, and smiled. Her appreciation for Guddu stemmed from his caring gestures. Sunita changed the topic. "So, have you thought more about it?" Guddu, torn between emotions, responded, "Why? Don't you think I can provide them with good school bags? I currently earn 5,000 to 6,000 rupees. Besides, I can relocate my business to Patna if we need more money." Sunita gently grasped Guddu's hand. "It's not about that, Guddu. Extra money is always good, but your earnings are split between you and your brother. This would be entirely ours. I could even send some extra money to my parents."

What motivates Guddu to finally wake up?
options_en: The smell of tea and litti

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Engaging in a deep and contemplative process, she took the time to carefully think as the various possibilities, considering various perspectives and potential outcomes before arriving at a well-considered and thoughtful decision.
options_en: Engaging in a deep and contemplative process,
considering various perspectives and potential outcomes
before arriving at a well-considered and thoughtful decision.
she took the time to carefully think as the various possibilities,
questions.solution_en:
Adverb 'as' cannot be used with- 'name, elect, think, consider, call, appoint, make, choose'. So, 'think as' will be changed to 'think about (give thought to)' in the given sentence.

The correct sentence is- "Engaging in a deep and contemplative process, she took the time to carefully think about the various possibilities, considering various perspectives and potential outcomes before arriving at a well-considered and thoughtful decision."

Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank(s).

France is ________ country but Australia is a continent as well as ______ country.
questions.solution_en:
The noun 'country' is singular in case of both the blanks. Moreover, it is a common noun representing a category. Thus, it will be preceded by the indefinite article 'a', in case of both the blanks. Hence, d) is the correct answer.

Note:

Definite and indefinite articles: In English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to, or introduces, a specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.
